definition.name: In, Inside, Into
definition.description: Use 'in' and 'inside' to show position in an area or space. Use 'into' to show movement from outside to inside. 'Inside' gives extra focus on the inner part, while 'in' is the most common neutral choice.

examples.english: The keys are in my bag.
examples.note: Use 'in' for position inside a container.
Use 'inside' to stress the inner part.

examples.english: The cat ran into the house.
examples.note: Use 'into' for movement from outside to inside.

examples.english: There is a lot of water in the bottle.
Come inside. It is cold outside.
examples.note: Here 'inside' is used as an adverb (no noun after it).

examples.english: She put her phone into her pocket.
examples.note: With verbs like 'put', use 'into' for direction.

expressions.meaning: in the inner part of the building
move from outside to the inside of the room
